Subject: HealthNet DPIA template — initial submission

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. We're running a DPIA as part of our vendor intake for an upcoming patient engagement feature and need Redwood to complete the attached DPIA template. Specifically we need:

- Completed DPIA sections (data categories, purpose, lawful basis, retention, processors/sub-processors)
- High-level data flow diagram showing where customer data and logs are stored/processed
- Evidence of relevant controls: SOC 2 Type II summary, network segmentation diagram, encryption at rest/in transit notes
- Clarification whether PHI or other special category health data may be processed on your hosted (SaaS) environment, or if that requires Private deployment + executed BAA

We've attached our template (HealthNet_DPIA_Template.xlsx) and a short list of mandatory evidentiary items. Can you confirm whether a response by end-of-day Friday 2025-11-07 is realistic, and whether your legal/compliance team needs additional details?

Thanks,

Hi Samantha — thanks for the template and the clear checklist. We can own this and assemble the evidence package. Quick responses and proposed timeline: 

- We will aim to return the completed DPIA and evidence by EOD Friday 2025-11-07 (UTC), though a small legal review may push final signed statements to Monday.
- PHI: our hosted public API is not intended for PHI by default. Customers with regulated health data normally deploy to Redwood Private (VPC / Dedicated) and we execute a BAA. I will confirm exact wording with Legal.
- Data flows & retention: Prash and Priyom will add a network/dataflow diagram and clarify default retention windows and log retention policies.

I'm looping in Priyom (Product Security) and Rishi (Legal) to supply the artifacts and any compliance language. If HealthNet can share which region(s) data will reside in (us-west / us-east / eu) that will help with the SCCs / DPA parts.

Subject: Re: HealthNet DPIA template — internal answers / evidence

Neha / team — following up with the artifacts and short answers so you can assemble the package to HealthNet.

Quick answers pulled into the template (high level):
- Data categories: customer-provided prompt text (customer content), metadata (timestamps, request id), derived embeddings/outputs. We do not by default collect or store PII beyond request metadata; customers can elect to store transcripts/logs.
- PHI handling: Redwood hosted (SaaS) is not approved for PHI. For customers who require PHI handling we support Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) and execute a BAA; this will be explicitly called out in the DPIA answer.
- Lawful basis: processing is per customer instruction (Art 6(1)(b)) for SaaS customers; where applicable, contractual necessity and legitimate interests for platform operations.
- Retention: default request/trace logs retained 30 days; artifacts (models/embeddings) not stored long-term unless customer enables persisted storage. Configurable retention available for Dedicated/Private.

Attachments included for the HealthNet packet:
- redwood_dpia_response.pdf — completed DPIA template with inline answers (PDF)
- SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf — control summary and link to full report under NDA
- network_dataflow_v2.png — high-level diagram (processing regions and sub-processors)

Notes for Legal: Rishi, I flagged the BAA catch — if HealthNet confirms PHI in scope we should offer Private + BAA and start template BAA review; standard turnaround ~7 business days for counter-sign. Also call-out that sub-processors (cloud infra providers) are listed in our DPA appendix; link included.

Let me know if you want me to redact any internal hostnames or produce an additional low-level diagram for HealthNet's security team.

-Priyom
Product Security | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

Samantha — attaching the completed DPIA responses and evidence package from our team. Summary below and next steps.

Summary of attachments: 
- redwood_dpia_response.pdf — completed template with our answers to HealthNet's questions (see sections 2, 4, 7 for PHI & retention language)
- SOC2_Type2_summary.pdf — condensed control report; full SOC2 Type II available under NDA (link in doc)
- network_dataflow_v2.png — high-level processing/dataflow diagram (shows regional processing and storage)

Key notes for HealthNet: 
- PHI: not supported on hosted public SaaS by default. If HealthNet needs PHI processing, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/Dedicated) and executing a BAA. We included suggested BAA language in section 7 of the PDF.
- Retention & logs: default 30-day retention for request traces; persistent storage requires configuration and may be subject to contract language.
- Sub-processors & SCCs: we provided a link in the package to our sub-processor list and DPA appendix; if HealthNet requires EU SCCs we will route through appropriate contractual addendum.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether PHI will be in scope (yes/no) and which region(s) you plan to host/operate in.
2) If you need the full SOC2 report we can provide via an NDA — I've included a Drive link and suggested HubSpot ticket for a formal request.
3) If acceptable, can you confirm receipt and whether any additional redlines are expected for the BAA/DPA?

HubSpot ticket: HS-12345678
